x: The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act was enacted in 1986.
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act came into force on December 23, 1986.
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act was majorly amended on September 1, 2016.
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act completely prohibits the employment of children below 14 years.
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act restricts adolescent work in hazardous processes.
The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act was enacted in 2005.
The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act came into force on February 15, 2006.
The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act constituted the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) as a statutory body.
The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act constituted State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCRs) as statutory bodies.
The NCPCR and SCPCRs monitor child welfare.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act was enacted in 2009.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act came into force on April 1, 2010.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14 years.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted in 2012.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act came into force on November 14, 2012.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was amended on August 16, 2019.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act is gender-neutral.
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act punishes child sexual abuse.
The 2019 amendment to the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act added capital punishment for aggravated penetrative assault.
The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act was enacted in 2015.
The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act came into force on January 15, 2016.
The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act was amended on September 1, 2022.
The Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act permits juveniles aged 16–18 years to be tried as adults for heinous crimes.
The 2021/2022 amendment to the Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act empowered District Magistrates (DMs) to issue adoption orders.

Name of the Act Year Date of Enforcement (Commencement) Note Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act 1986 December 23, 1986 (Major Amendment: Sept 1, 2016) Complete prohibition of employment of children below 14; restricts adolescent work in hazardous processes. Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act 2005 February 15, 2006 Constituted NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies for child welfare monitoring. Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act 2015 January 15, 2016 (Amended: Sept 1, 2022) Permits trial of juveniles aged 16–18 as adults for heinous crimes; 2021/2022 amendment empowered DMs for adoption orders.

x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act (PCR) was enacted in 1955.
The Protection of Civil Rights Act came into force on June 1, 1955.
The Protection of Civil Rights Act was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability Offences Act.
The Protection of Civil Rights Act enforces Article 17 of the Constitution.
The Protection of Civil Rights Act prescribes penalties for practicing untouchability.
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in 1989.
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act came into force on January 30, 1990.
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was amended on August 20, 2018.
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act prevents atrocities.
Section 18A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act bars anticipatory bail.
Section 18A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act removes the requirement of a preliminary inquiry before arrest.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act is also known as PESA.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act was enacted in 1996.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act came into force on December 24, 1996.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act extends Part IX of the Constitution to Schedule V areas.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act empowers traditional Gram Sabhas.
The Forest Rights Act is also known as FRA.
The Forest Rights Act was enacted in 2006.
The Forest Rights Act came into force on December 31, 2007.
The rules under the Forest Rights Act were notified on January 1, 2008.
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes.
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes.
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was enacted in 2007.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act came into force through a state-wise notification rollout beginning on December 29, 2007.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act places a legal maintenance obligation on children.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act places a legal maintenance obligation on heirs.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act empowers Maintenance Tribunals.
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act was enacted in 2013.
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act came into force on December 6, 2013.
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act totally bans manual cleaning of unsanitary latrines without protective gear.
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act totally bans manual cleaning of open drains without protective gear.
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act totally bans manual cleaning of sewers without protective gear.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act is also known as the RPwD Act.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was enacted in 2016.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act came into force on April 19, 2017.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act replaced the 1995 Act.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act expanded the disability categories from 7 to 21.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act provides 4% reservation in public employment.
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act provides 5% reservation in higher education.

Name of the Act Year Date of Enforcement (Commencement) Note Protection of Civil Rights Act (PCR) 1955 June 1, 1955 (Renamed in 1976 from Untouchability Offences Act) Enforces Article 17; prescribes penalties for practicing untouchability. Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA) 1996 December 24, 1996 Extends Part IX of Constitution to Schedule V areas, empowering traditional Gram Sabhas. Forest Rights Act (FRA) 2006 December 31, 2007 (Rules notified: Jan 1, 2008) Vests individual and community forest rights in forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 December 29, 2007 (State-wise notification rollout) Legal maintenance obligation on children/heirs; empowers Maintenance Tribunals. Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers & their Rehabilitation Act 2013 December 6, 2013 Total ban on manual cleaning of unsanitary latrines, open drains, and sewers without protective gear. Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016 April 19, 2017 Replaced 1995 Act; expanded disability categories from 7 to 21; provides 4% reservation in public employment and 5% in higher education.

x: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act was enacted in 1991.
The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act came into force on July 11, 1991.
The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act freezes the religious character of places of worship as they existed on August 15, 1947.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act was enacted in 2024.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act came into force on June 21, 2024.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act curbs paper leaks in central recruitment and entrance tests.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act curbs organized cheating in central recruitment and entrance tests.
The offense under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act is non-bailable.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) was enacted in 2023.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) came into force on July 1, 2024.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced IPC 1860.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) includes dedicated provisions on crimes against women and children.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) includes dedicated provisions on organized crime.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) includes dedicated provisions on mob lynching.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was enacted in 2023.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) came into force on July 1, 2024.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replaced CrPC 1973.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) establishes digital forensics.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) establishes statutory Zero FIR.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) establishes strict investigation timeframes.

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 July 1, 2024 Replaced CrPC 1973; establishes digital forensics, statutory Zero FIR, and strict investigation timeframes.
